name: Curator
description: Asks an LLM what your library has in common and builds the answers into ordered playlists surfaced as home screen rows.
overview: LLM-inferred vibe categories for your Jellyfin library.

versions.changelog:
Adds a Footer tab: a footer drawn at the bottom of Jellyfin itself, with a heading, a line of text and a row of link buttons. Shown on the home screen by default, or on every page if you prefer. Off by default, and it needs the File Transformation plugin to do the drawing — because the fragment is stored in that plugin's configuration rather than held in memory, it survives restarts on its own. Everything you type is written into the page as text rather than markup, and link addresses are limited to http, https, mailto and same-server paths.

The weather and time-of-day row now titles itself in Title Case, matching Jellyfin's own rows — "Good for an Overcast Afternoon" rather than "Good for an overcast afternoon". Existing titles are re-made on the next hourly refresh.

The condensing pass no longer treats two library rows for one title as two things to summarise — it was the last place in the plugin that did, so a library holding a show twice paid for two rewrites and listed it twice. A new 'Remove duplicates' button on the Summaries tab clears the ones already stored without waiting for the next daily pass. It uses the same duplicate test as the rest of the plugin, never a title match, so two different films sharing a name are safe; nothing is bought and nothing is lost, since a summary removed in error is re-made next pass.

Adds a 'Prune empty playlists' action on the Runs tab and a daily 'Prune Empty Playlists' scheduled task. Jellyfin re-imports playlist folders left on disk after their playlists were deleted, and they arrive with no owner, no contents and none of Curator's marks — so they sit beside your real playlists as empty duplicates that nothing was allowed to clean up. The sweep removes those and Curator's own empties, along with the leftover folder so a later scan cannot bring them back. It never touches a playlist with anything in it, and never touches an untagged playlist that has an owner: that one is yours, empty or not. The button requires a second confirming click and lists exactly what will go first.

The weather and time-of-day row no longer announces a clear sky. 'Good for a clear evening' says barely more than 'Good for an evening', so a plain clear sky is left out and the hour carries the title; a clear sky with heat or cold is still named, because a cold bright morning is a specific thing. Every other condition — rain, snow, storm, fog, overcast, hot, cold — is named as before. Titles bought under the old wording are replaced on the next hourly refresh.
